prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a continuous, upward-sloping ground plane receding from a bright foreground about 1 m in front of and below the camera wearer to a dark background more than 15–20 m away, with a sidewalk edge on the left and a vertical tree trunk on the right that approaches from roughly 8 m in frame 1 to 4 m in frame 5. No people are visible in the scene, while a small dog on a leash stands directly in front of and below the camera wearer at roughly 1.2–1.5 m (just beyond arm's reach, though the proximal end of the leash is within arm's reach at the bottom left), positioned 3–7 m in front of and to the left of the approaching tree trunk. Across frames 1 to 4, the dog turns its head from facing right to facing forward-left and lowers its body while the camera wearer advances closer to it (down to about 1 m in frame 4), until the dog drops completely out of the lower frame edge in frame 5 and only a tiny segment of the leash remains at the bottom-left corner. Compared to the uniform white snow in the RGB strip, the depth map makes the smooth distance gradient of the snowbank, the slight step down to the sidewalk on the left, and the exact 3D relief of the thin leash and tree trunks much easier to see. However, the map is unreliable along the thin leash—which falsely merges with the adjacent snow surface in thickness—and in the distant upper-left street and houses beyond 15 m, which flatten into uniform black with lost structural detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few disconnected regions against a black background: the foreground dog at 1–1.5 m below and in front of the camera wearer in frames 1–3, and distant background regions on the upper left roughly 15–30 m away (about 14–28 m behind and to the left of the dog). In the RGB scene, no people are present, yet the segmentation map misclassifies the foreground dog as a 'person' in frames 1 and 2 and as a 'cat' in frame 3, while completely missing the dog in frame 4 as it crouches lower at 1 m and in frame 5 after it exits the bottom of the view. In the upper-left background, parked cars and houses along the street are sporadically mislabelled as tiny 'person' instances in frame 1 and large 'train' masks in frames 3 and 4, before three parked cars at roughly 15–25 m on the left are correctly segmented as 'car' instances in frame 5 (partially occluding one another in a row along the curb). While the masks in frames 1–3 provide a sharp silhouette of the animal's rightward-then-leftward head orientation and frame 5 helps separate the overlapping distant cars from the dark street trees in the RGB image, the map is highly unreliable overall due to severe class hallucinations, complete omission of the leash, trees, and snow, and missing detections in frame 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank black across the five frames, containing only two small, erroneous yellow body skeletons at the bottom foreground in frames 1 and 3 where the dog is located roughly 1.2–1.5 m in front of and below the camera wearer. Because no humans or visible hands are in the field of view (the camera wearer's hands holding the leash remain out of frame below the lower edge), there are no true human orientations, gazes toward the camera, or interpersonal distances to represent. In frame 1, the false skeleton aligns vertically along the left side of the dog's back and rightward-turned head, and in frame 3 a compact, folded yellow skeleton appears on the dog's hunched torso as it faces forward-left, while frames 2, 4, and 5 contain no detections at all. This map adds no useful spatial information beyond the RGB image and is unreliable because the pose estimator misfires on the dark silhouette of the dog against the white snow in two frames while failing to represent the scene's actual non-human geometry.
